memories.author: patient
memories.text: I am a 39‑year‑old school bus driver living in Malleshwaram. For the past 6 months I have trouble falling asleep, waking up tired, and I have daily itchy wheals that worsen in the evenings. I also feel irritable during shifts.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Insomnia and chronic urticaria.
Evidence: patient reports sleep onset latency >45 min, daytime fatigue, and daily pruritic wheals with evening exacerbation. Physical examination shows mild periorbital pallor, no lung wheals, skin shows scattered erythematous papules.
Smoking status: never smoker, pack‑years 0.
Plan: start melatonin 3 mg at bedtime, trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for sleep; levocetirizine 5 mg each morning and cetirizine 10 mg at night for urticaria. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Melatonin 3 mg HS

Levocetirizine 5 mg OD
Cetirizine 10 mg HS

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
TSH 2.1 mIU/L (0.4‑4.0)
Haemoglobin 12.8 g/dL (12.0‑15.5)
CBC: WBC 6.2x10^9/L, Neutrophils 4.0, Lymphocytes 1.8, Eosinophils 0.3x10^9/L (0.0‑0.5)
Insomnia Severity Index score 14 (moderate)

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Sleep has worsened; I now take >1 hour to fall asleep and wake twice nightly. The hives are more intense, especially after stress at work, and I need extra antihistamine to control itching.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Insomnia and chronic urticaria – not well controlled.
Evidence: ISI now 18, patient reports delayed sleep onset and nocturnal awakenings; wheals appear daily with increased size and pruritus. Examination shows mild facial puffiness, skin shows widespread urticarial plaques.
Smoking status: never smoker, pack‑years 0.
Plan: increase trazodone to 75 mg HS, keep melatonin 3 mg HS; raise levocetirizine to 10 mg OD and continue cetirizine 10 mg HS. Add short‑term leukotriene receptor antagonist if needed. Review in 4 weeks.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-10-03 at 10:00 with Dr Suresh Menon (D05).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Insomnia and chronic urticaria – improving.
Evidence: ISI down to 12, patient reports sleep onset ~30 min, fewer nocturnal awakenings; wheals reduced to 2‑3 per week, milder. Examination shows clear lungs, skin shows only occasional faint papules.
Smoking status: never smoker, pack‑years 0.
Plan: stop trazodone, continue melatonin 3 mg HS; maintain levocetirizine 5 mg OD and cetirizine 10 mg HS. Review in 3 months.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: After the New Year holidays my sleep got worse again; I’m waking up feeling unrefreshed. The hives flared after eating shellfish at a family meal, needing extra antihistamine.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Insomnia and chronic urticaria – mild exacerbation.
Evidence: ISI 14, patient reports delayed sleep onset and fatigue; wheals appear 4‑5 days/week after trigger foods. Examination shows mild periorbital dark circles, skin shows scattered urticarial lesions.
Smoking status: never smoker, pack‑years 0.
Plan: restart trazodone 50 mg HS, keep melatonin 3 mg HS; increase levocetirizine to 10 mg OD, continue cetirizine 10 mg HS. Review in 6 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Insomnia and chronic urticaria – well controlled.
Evidence: ISI 9, patient reports sleep onset <20 min, refreshed waking; wheals rare, only occasional mild patches after stress. Examination normal.
Smoking status: never smoker, pack‑years 0.
Plan: consider tapering trazodone to 25 mg HS if symptoms stay stable, continue melatonin and antihistamines as needed. Review in 3 months.
